# CLIENT BRIEF — HÔTEL LYNX, AGADIR (verbatim intent from the client; binding; do not edit)

## Core idea
DO NOT turn Lynx into a fake luxury hotel. That would be creatively lazy and commercially stupid. Its strength appears to be almost the opposite: **simple accommodation done really well.**

Public reputation suggests: clean · useful location · helpful staff · good value · straightforward rooms · Wi-Fi · parking · practical city base. So make THAT feel cool. The website should make an honest independent two-star hotel feel incredibly confident.

Think: **Your base in Agadir.** Not: "An oasis of unparalleled luxury."

## Current public baseline (research thoroughly and verify)
- Hôtel Lynx / Hotel Lynx
- address approximately: 9 Rue al Mahdi ibn Toumart, Talborjt / Swiss City, Agadir 80000
- publicly classified around 2 stars
- Booking rating approximately 8.5, around 1,000+ Booking reviews; staff ≈9.2, cleanliness ≈8.9, value ≈8.8, location ≈8.9; Wi-Fi particularly well rated
- free parking · 24-hour front desk · room service · terrace · air conditioning · private bathrooms · TV / satellite channels
- approximately 20-minute walk to Agadir Beach; restaurants/services nearby
- Current public room listings have included at least: single room, double room. RESEARCH COMPLETE CURRENT ROOM INVENTORY.
- Some public evidence suggests breakfast may NOT currently be offered. VERIFY THIS. Do not invent breakfast because hotels "normally" have it.

## Creative thesis
A potentially fantastic branding direction around: **No nonsense. Good sleep. Agadir outside.** (not necessarily those words). The design can almost have an anti-resort confidence. Things that matter: room is clean · people are helpful · Wi-Fi works · parking exists · location is useful · price is sensible · city/beach are accessible. Make practicality feel desirable.

## Possible homepage
strong honest property hero · "Your base in Agadir" · rooms · practical amenities · why guests return · neighbourhood · how far from key places · reviews · parking / Wi-Fi / reception · availability inquiry.

## Rooms
Use REAL imagery. Do not create misleading luxury through fake assets. Good design should elevate the actual rooms without misrepresenting them. Show useful things: beds · occupancy · bathroom · AC · Wi-Fi · TV · room size if verified · view if applicable · accessibility if verified.

## Neighbourhood
This could become the coolest part of the site. Research the immediate area properly. Build something like **Your Agadir from Lynx**. Show verified nearby: restaurants · cafés · shops · beach · taxis · useful landmarks · promenade · attractions. Use actual walking/driving times only when accurate. Make Lynx feel like a good jumping-off point rather than merely a room.

## Direct availability
Do not fake a PMS. A polished inquiry is enough: arrival · departure · guests · room preference · phone / WhatsApp · email · arrival time · parking needed. If a current Booking.com link exists, that can be secondary.

## Visual identity
Modern city hotel. Graphic. Crisp. Honest. Confident. Potentially use the Lynx name subtly: eye-line · geometry · sharp editorial cuts. DO NOT plaster cartoon cats everywhere. Avoid fake gold luxury. Avoid generic travel beige.

This site should make somebody think: **"Why does this inexpensive hotel have such a ridiculously good website?"** That is exactly the point.

## Cross-site test
Lynx must feel like **confident, practical, excellent-value urban hospitality** — clearly different from Hala Tours (a local world of experiences) and Line Up Surf House (rhythm of surfing).

## Owner embarrassment test
Would Lynx say "We don't have breakfast / that room / that amenity"? Fix anything uncertain.
